# A late article response can overwrite the selected Portal page

## Context

Portal Learning, Blog and Release pages load the selected article through `Neo.app.content.Component`. Timeline pages duplicate its fetch so they can observe timeline items.

## The Problem

On `dev` `50fcfc526c`, real component instances with held response bodies reproduce A → B → A using the same Store record for both A visits. A from the last visit publishes first, then A from the first visit overwrites it. Clearing the route or destroying the component while a body is pending also lets the obsolete request reach the observer. An earlier route’s deferred scroll can run after the next route starts.

## The Architectural Reality

Design authority: `Component.record` binds to `currentPageRecord`. The shared content component owns writing the fetched Markdown and scrolling after navigation. The timeline’s alternate selector can use the same load and settlement path.

## The Fix

Track the current article request in the shared component. Compare the request identity after the body resolves and after the scroll delay. A clear or destroy prevents late effects. Keep the timeline’s observer selector when it adopts the shared loader.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Under controlled A → B → A completion, only the latest A body publishes and observes headings.
- [ ] A cleared or destroyed view discards a delayed response. A delayed scroll from the previous route does not scroll the current route.
- [ ] The timeline uses the same loader with its timeline item selector. Focused content and Markdown tests pass.

## Out of Scope

Markdown’s independent asynchronous rendering stages and Portal content composition.
